verdict.rationale: Google's own GitHub repository says the project includes open-source one-time passcode generator implementations for several mobile platforms, so some client code that handles seeds can be inspected. Nothing in the evidence ties that repo to the currently shipped app, which the docs describe with Google Account cloud sync and Privacy Screen, so it is unproven that the code users actually run is the code published. Missing for 10: evidence that the current shipping iOS/Android apps (including sync and seed-storage code) are open source, any evidence of community review or audits of the client code, and licensing/reproducibility details.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the client apps are open source, so the code handling my seeds can be inspected and community-reviewed

citations.quote: The Google Authenticator project includes implementations of one-time passcode generators for several mobile platforms.
These implementations support the HMAC-Based One-time Password (HOTP) algorithm specified in RFC 4226 and the Time-based One-time Password (TOTP) algorithm specified in RFC 6238.
